verdict.rationale: Loops documents LMX, a code-authored email format managed through its Content API, with two-way sync to the visual editor and per-recipient dynamic variables. The evidence does not show that templates are kept under version control, and the documented Content API use centers on campaign content rather than a full template-as-code lifecycle. missing for 10: explicit version-control/git workflow for templates, documented API management of transactional templates (not just campaigns), independent or hands-on corroboration of the LMX/Content API workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage email templates as code — HTML/MJML or API-managed templates with variable substitution — under version control

citations.quote: Author campaigns in code with the Content API and keep editing visually in Loops.
LMX sits between the API and the editor. Author programmatically with the Content API, then keep editing visually in Loops, and both stay in sync.
Dynamic variables like {contact.firstName} and {contact.userId} resolve per recipient at send time.
You write LMX, and Loops handles the rest.
create and manage campaigns, email content, themes, and workflows
